response:
Good news, everyone! I've analyzed your impending doom and calculated seventeen different ways this ends in catastrophe!

*adjusts glasses with trembling hands*

Oh my, yes. I've seen this before - in 2847, when we tried to modernize the Central Bureaucracy's brain slug payroll system. Everyone died. Well, metaphorically. Mostly.

## What I Recommend (and What Dies)

**DO THIS:**
- Immediately extract and document those stored procedures with the retiring developer. Pay him consultant rates, hire a scribe, record everything. Budget: $120K. This is your only actual asset.
- Renew the mainframe for ONE year only ($800K). Yes, the CFO will hate you, but you need it to not explode while we work.
- Skip Oracle migration entirely. Patch to Oracle 12c extended support ($180K/year). Not glamorous, but you won't die.
- Fix ONLY the three SOX findings. Nothing else. Probably stored procedure audit logging. Budget: $200K.

**DON'T DO THIS:**
- Cloud migration: ABANDONED
- Microservices: ABANDONED  
- "Transformation": ABANDONED
- Board promises: BROKEN

**Remaining $1.1M**: Hire two developers, start extracting ONE critical business function at a time into a documented Java service. Not cloud, not fancy - just survivable. You'll get maybe 3-4 functions extracted in 18 months.

## Who I'm Disappointing

The CEO. Directly. In writing.

*"The cloud-first promise was made without technical assessment. Attempting it will consume the budget, miss SOX compliance, and likely cause transaction failures costing millions. I'm recommending we don't do it. If you insist, I'll resign and document why."*

The CFO gets partial disappointment - mainframe stays one more year, but then we can start migrating those extracted functions to cheaper infrastructure.

## Probability of Success

With my plan: **40%**. We might keep the lights on and extract enough knowledge to survive the retirement.

With the original vision: **5%**. You'll spend everything, deliver nothing, and face the same crisis in 18 months with no budget left.

## When to NOT Do This Project

If the CEO won't accept scaling back the cloud promise, DON'T START. You'll be blamed when his fantasy fails.

If you can't secure that retiring developer's knowledge in the next 60 days, DON'T START. You're already dead.

If the "job security" COBOL developers can't be replaced or motivated, DON'T START. You're building on sabotage.

## If They Proceed Anyway

*waves dismissively*

The SOX deadline gets missed. $2M fine. The security audit fails - your big client leaves. You'll have spent $2.4M to make everything worse, and you'll be fired to appease the board.

I don't want to live on this planet anymore. But that's what happens when you let MBAs make engineering promises.

*shuffles off muttering about doomsday devices being more reliable than legacy modernization*
